passages.provision_quote: For any employee who customarily and regularly receives tips or gratuities from patrons or others, the employer may pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute if the employer can establish by the employer's records of charged tips or gratuities or by the employee’s declaration for federal insurance contributions act purposes that for each week, when adding tips or gratuities received to wages paid, the employee received not less than the minimum wage plus $2 for all hours worked.

rows.reasoning: Mesnard prime-sponsored and voted yes on SCR1040 (2024), but its operative section lets an employer "pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute" only where tips bring the worker to "not less than the minimum wage plus $2" — a tip-credit mechanism for one category of worker. That changes neither the statutory floor's level nor the mechanism by which it is adjusted, which is what the rungs differ on. It therefore cannot separate "Hold the wage floor at its current level and let the market set pay above it." from "Remove the wage floor entirely and let employers and workers set pay by agreement." or from the rungs that raise the floor, so no passage survives V2 and the row is blank.
